L32: ## 【15†noun】
L33: 
L34: dash·​board 【16†ˈdash-ˌbȯrd 】
L35: 
L36: plural dashboards
L37: 
L38: Simple Definition A Simple Definition is available from our Learner's Dictionary to help you understand the meaning faster.
L39: 
L40: 1
L41: 
L42: : a panel extending across the interior of a vehicle (such as an automobile) below the windshield and usually containing instruments and controls
L43: 
L44: If something internal is wrong with your car, the dashboard will display an icon identifying the problem.—Aaron Widmar
L45: Abdullah sang along to the songs; I kept the rhythm by clapping my hands and drumming on the dashboard.—Emma Sky
L46: 
L47: 2
L48: 
L49: : a graphical report (as on a website) of various data relevant to a particular business, group, etc.
L50: 
L51: … other dashboards that are available for first-year applicants include information on admission by source school …—Daily Californian
L52: The dashboard provides data on regional, local and campus trends regarding COVID-19 testing, results and cases. The dashboard is updated each weekday with data from several different sources, including the campus testing program and self-reports by students and faculty.—Alex Perry
L53: 
L54: Emory Police Department (EPD) will implement a dashboard of the department's data, including the status and findings of investigations and the demographics of those involved …—Ninad Kulkarni
L55: The RTA [Regional Transportation Authority of Northeastern Illinois] uses maps and dashboards to visualize revenue, ridership, and service availability at a regional scale.—Terry Bills
L56: 
L57: 3
L58: 
L59: : a screen on the front of a usually horse-drawn vehicle to intercept water, mud, or snow
